outcome.body.collapse: The “{family}” crisis reached 100. The communities go their separate ways. Your Legacy carries over to the next civilization.

policy.queuedDecision: Order queued. Open “Review dilemma” and choose a response to unblock time.
outcome.body.darkFirst: The “{family}” crisis broke the institutions. {name} stays in Prehistory. Rebuild with the era’s starting policies, from the current year.
absence.restoring: Catching up: {percent}% of your available offline time simulated.
absence.finalReady: Your civilization is ready for Transcendence. In Settlement, choose “Complete transcendence” when you are ready.
absence.duration: Time away: {away} (min:sec). Simulation ran for {active} at {speed}×.
compat.desktop: Play Epoche on a computer with a keyboard and mouse.
compat.browsers: Epoche has been tested on desktop Chrome and Firefox.
slot.writeError: Save failed. You can export your progress.
slot.captureError: Current progress could not be captured.

era.change.prehistory: Groups follow the game they hunt. Establishing a permanent camp prepares the way for the Neolithic.
era.change.neolithic: Crops and granaries sustain growth. The way land is managed decides how much food survives a poor year.
era.change.bronze: Furnaces open the metals trade. Tribute and territorial defence become practical choices.
era.change.classical: The city gives law and defence to distinct institutions. Who holds power decides who gets heard.
era.change.medieval: Walls, faiths and land bind local communities. The loyalty of different groups matters as much as control of resources.
era.change.earlymodern: Print and trade routes carry ideas farther. The city decides who can take part in the new exchanges.
era.change.industrial: Workshops and factories increase output. Health, working conditions and city air bear the cost.
era.change.contemporary: Schools, services and infrastructure support an urban population. Public decisions allocate access and costs.
era.change.information: Networks speed up learning and coordination. Policies decide who controls the data.
era.change.future: The city can sustain life beyond the valley. Its last choices decide what knowledge travels with it.
log.era: {name} reaches {era}. The chronicle resumes in the new period after a jump in time.
outcome.body.dark: The crisis “{family}” broke the institutions. Entering the dark age returns {name} to the technologies and policies of the preceding era. The campaign continues from the same year.
outcome.body.fragment: The crisis “{family}” split {name} into two communities. The one you follow keeps 62% of the population and some land. The other becomes a neighbouring civilization.
outcome.body.conquest: {rival} prevailed. Migrating means taking over the victor, with its population and lands. Staying keeps your people, reduces the population by a third and pauses decisions for a period of dormancy.
outcome.body.extinction: The crisis “{family}” left too few people for the campaign to continue. The Legacy earned so far carries over to future civilizations.
outcome.body.transcendence: {name} achieved Transcendence after meeting the Future era’s conditions. The campaign ends and its Legacy passes to future civilizations.
world.truceBreak: Breaking the truce costs {cost} extra Influence and damages relations.
world.pact.effect.trade: Trade strengthens sustenance and opens regular commerce.
world.pact.effect.truce: A truce limits hostilities for a set period.
world.pact.effect.alliance: An alliance preserves trade and strengthens defence.
world.pact.effect.aid: Aid improves relations and temporarily supports the neighbour's food supply and health.
world.objective.effect.defend: A victory boosts Cohesion for a time. A defeat can cost you a territory.
world.objective.effect.tribute: Victory imposes a tribute that supports resources and Influence.
world.objective.effect.conquer: Victory transfers control of a territory. More territories sustain more people.
